name: Certified Parts Corporation
old_description: Certified Parts Corporation (CPC) was founded in 1982 by James Grafft, with a mission to preserve well known international and local legacy brands that were in danger of extinction.  Initially specializing in manufacturing service parts for these companies, CPC has grown into a major supplier to OEM’s and has brought some of these brands back into production. Comet, TecumsehPower, Wisconsin Wagon and vintage recreational vehicle parts makeup CPC’s current lineup of companies.  CPC owns motorcycles and mini-cycle brands that include Bridgestone and Indian, Rupp, Chaparral and Steen along with a complimentary selection of hard-to-get engine parts that were used in many of the snowmobiles and mini-cycles of the day. A passion for history and recognizing opportunity serves as a guiding principle for Certified Parts Corporation.
about:
Certified Parts Corporation (CPC) was founded in 1982 by James Grafft in Edgerton, Wisconsin. The company began with a mission to preserve well-known international and local legacy brands facing extinction. Grafft’s experience at Fox Corporation in Janesville, where he saw the need for continuous parts supply for defunct manufacturers, led him to purchase the service parts division when Fox shut down in 1976. He later acquired the Bridgestone brand on his 26th birthday and established CPC in 1982, acquiring the Arctic Cat snowmobile division from bankruptcy.

Today, CPC operates a 200,000-square-foot factory in Edgerton where it manufactures original service parts, including carburetors and the full line of Comet torque converters and clutches. The company acquires legacy brands—such as TecumsehPower, Comet, Hoffco, Wisconsin Wagon, and vintage recreational vehicle lines—and restarts production of their components. It also manages extensive parts inventories and provides distribution and service support through a worldwide dealer network.

CPC serves OEMs and aftermarket customers in recreational, construction, agricultural, and marine industries. Its brand portfolio includes snowmobile, mini-cycle, watercraft, and outdoor power equipment lines. Concrete examples include supplying Comet clutches to OEM manufacturers across multiple sectors and supporting engines for snowmobiles, mini-cycles, and utility equipment through the Lauson, Snow King, and LCT brands.

The company’s guiding principle is a passion for history and recognizing opportunity in orphaned brands. By acquiring intellectual property, tooling, and inventory, CPC keeps legacy products running and reintroduces historic names to the market, such as the 1895 Lauson engine line.
